items.summary: The webapp-testing skill equips agents to verify local web applications using native Python Playwright scripts and bundled server lifecycle helpers. A decision tree routes static HTML tasks to direct file inspection, while dynamic apps use scripts/with_server.py to start one or more dev servers before automation runs. The reconnaissance-then-action pattern navigates, waits for networkidle, captures screenshots or DOM snapshots, discovers selectors, then executes actions against the rendered state. Documentation stresses running helper scripts with --help first and treating them as black boxes to avoid loading large source into context. Examples cover element discovery, static HTML file URLs, and console log capture under the examples directory. Best practices require headless Chromium, explicit browser cleanup, descriptive selectors, and waiting for networkidle before inspecting dynamic single-page apps. Developers reach for it when verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing screenshots, or reading browser logs during local development test cycles.

Reference files link MCP best practices, language guides, protocol docs, evaluation scripts, and SDK README sources for both languages.
highlights: Four-phase workflow: research and planning, implementation, review and test, and LLM evaluation design.
